publicly_readable: One article, reprinted on worldin.economist.com in 2015 for the 30th edition ("The World in 1987: A political outlook", by Andrew Boyd), read from an Internet Archive snapshot.
not_readable: Everything else in the issue. No other text of this edition was found in public form.

entries.quote: Note first, a couple of things that will not happen in 1987. The Americans will not send up any space shuttles.
entries.subject: Space Shuttle flights resume

entries.quote: The Russians will not repair the radioactive wreckage at Chernobyl.
entries.subject: Chernobyl reactor repair
entries.note: Framed as permanent, not only for 1987.

entries.quote: it has to be assumed that Colonel Qaddafi will still be around in 1987
entries.subject: Qaddafi remains in power

entries.quote: Reagan will not scrap the SDI except as part of a comprehensive arms reduction deal, which shows no sign of emerging in 1987.
entries.subject: Strategic Defence Initiative and comprehensive arms deal

entries.quote: In 1987 the Russians will not agree to pull back a third of a million solders
entries.subject: Soviet troop withdrawals demanded by China

entries.quote: This is the strongest reason for expecting that 1987, while it will produce no historic breakthrough in east-west relations, will see further movements long the arms control road – modest movements, with continued creaking and straining, but perceptible ones.
entries.subject: US-Soviet arms control 1987

entries.quote: “1987”, proclaimed the cover of the very first TWI, would see (among other things) “a nasty shock for Mrs Thatcher”, “a last-ditch push by America's moral majority” and “a Japanese takeover of a major Wall Street firm”.
entries.subject: Cover-line predictions for 1987
entries.note: Restated in "Looking back on the future" (The World in 2006), a review by an outside historian; the original wording is not seen. The cover lines are quoted.

entries.quote: he predicted that Nomura Securities would take over Merrill Lynch.
entries.subject: Nomura takeover of Merrill Lynch
entries.note: Restated in "Looking back on the future" (The World in 2006), a review by an outside historian; the original wording is not seen.

notes: Edition number counted from The World in 1987 = 1. Publication month not confirmed; year only. The reprint is The Economist's own web copy of the original article. This is the first edition of the series; the World in 2016 index page calls it "the first edition of The World In...".
